text:
martin.h: Heads-up — after the autotune push yesterday I see a 10-15% P95 increase for requests around 128/256 tokens. Only in hosted region eu-west-1, prefill-heavy workloads.

sara.k: Ugh. Is that on prefill or decode path?

martin.h: Looks like prefill. Decode-only paths for long ctx are fine.

leo: Any changes to kernel selection heuristics in the autotune? I remember we added an architecture-aware fallback for Ampere->Hopper picks.

martin.h: Yes, autotune switched to the "unified-concat" kernel for sequences >= 120 on Hopper because microbenchmarks showed better throughput. But the real workload distribution has many 64+ prefix tokens then decode of 32 tokens. Seems we misclassified those as long-prefill.

rina: That sounds like the classic boundary problem. Are we using the session-level max_seq to pick kernels?

martin.h: We use the max_seq in the sample window. If > threshold, pick unified-concat. But because we were sampling across batched requests, mid-length tails push the sampled max above 120.

leo: Can you paste the kernel selection pseudocode?

martin.h: Sure — here's the simplified flow we're running:

```
// pick kernel for prefill
int max_seq = sample_max(window);
if (is_hopper && max_seq >= 120) {
  kernel = K_UNIFIED_CONCAT; // fast for long continuous prefill
} else if (quantized) {
  kernel = K_Q8_SPLIT;
} else {
  kernel = K_BASE;
}
```

martin.h: Problem is sample_max(window) includes a few long-chat sessions that are decode-heavy but still count in prefill sampling. So prefill requests for short ones get routed to K_UNIFIED_CONCAT which has worse latency for short-batched prefill (higher setup cost + different memory access).

sara.k: Do we have KV cache eviction interactions? Maybe the unified path forces a different KV layout and evicts hot entries for the next decode?

martin.h: Good catch. Profiling shows increased KV cache misses for affected requests. Here's a small perf snippet from perfview (prefill short case):

```
P95 latency: +12%
KV cache hits: 82% -> 61%
avg batch size: 3.1 -> 3.3
kernel_setup_ms: 0.8 -> 2.1
```

leo: kernel_setup_ms jump is telling. Unified concat does extra reorg on KV buffers. For small prefill it dominates.

rina: Two angles: change sampling to separate prefill/decode histograms, or use per-request heuristics (if request.seq < 96 prefer short kernel). Which is faster to revert?

sara.k: We could also add a small classifier at runtime: if (prefill && seq_mean < 100) route to short-prefill path regardless of sampled max. Cheap fix.

martin.h: I can roll a fix: modify autotuner to maintain two histograms: prefill_max and decode_max and make kernel pick use the prefill histogram when deciding prefill kernels. That keeps decode-driven long sessions from influencing prefill picks.

leo: Sounds safer. Also add KV-cache-aware cost: kernel weight += kv_eviction_penalty when deciding. Autotune's cost model currently only considers throughput and setup; we should include estimated KV churn.

rina: For rollout, do a canary in eu-west-1 where regression was seen. Add trace flags so we collect: per-request kernel_chosen, seq_len, is_prefill, kv_hits, kernel_setup_ms.

martin.h: Agreed. Plan:
1) Quick patch: prefer short-prefill kernel when request.seq < 96 (hotfix) — deploy in 30m to canary.
2) Longer: split histograms + KV penalty in autotuner (next release).
3) Add perf traces and a dashboard for kernel selection mismatches.

deploy-bot: deploy request: martin.h/dev/short-prefill-fix -> canary/eu-west-1 queued. :rocket:

leo: Also add unit test that simulates mixed workload: many decode-heavy long sessions + many short prefill requests, ensure prefill picks short kernel.

martin.h: Will do. I'll post the perf traces after the canary runs. Thanks for the quick triage. :pray:

rina: FYI, this also explains a support ticket where one customer saw tail spikes at similar times. I'll coordinate.

martin.h: Last note — we should avoid tying kernel choice solely to sample_max(window). Maybe use a percentile (90th) and split by path. That should reduce sensitivity to outliers.

leo: Agreed. Great catch, Martin.

martin.h: Uploading a short trace bundle to /tmp and will attach to the ticket.

sara.k: Nice. Keep us posted. :thumbsup:
